Mobile Balance and Data Check Codes for All Pakistani Networks

All-network USSD codes to check balance, data, SMS and packages in Pakistan 2026: Jazz and Telenor *111#, Ufone *706#, Zong *102#, plus PTA helpline 0800-55055.

Photo: Redolta · CC0 · source

Short answer: Each Pakistani network has a self-care short code for balance, data and packages. Jazz and Telenor commonly use *111#, Ufone uses *706# and Zong uses *102#. Dial the code, follow the on-screen menu, and verify the result with the network or the PTA.

The self-care short codes

Every Pakistani operator offers a self-care menu that shows your balance, remaining data, SMS and active packages. The exact menu changes over time, so treat these codes as a starting point and confirm the current one with your network.

  • Jazz: commonly dial *111# for the self-care menu.
  • Telenor: commonly dial *111# for the self-care menu.
  • Ufone: commonly dial *706# for balance and package information.
  • Zong: commonly dial *102# for balance and package information.

After dialling, choose the option for balance, data or bundles from the on-screen list. Most of these services are free, but always check the menu wording before confirming a chargeable action.

How to use a USSD code

  1. Open the dialler on the phone holding the SIM.
  2. Type the code for your network and press call.
  3. Read the menu that appears on screen.
  4. Reply with the number of the option you want, such as balance or data.

USSD menus need an active network signal but do not use mobile data. If the menu freezes, close the dialler and dial again.

Check your own SIM number

If you also need the number of the SIM you are using, each network has a quick check: Telenor *8888#, Jazz *99#, Ufone *7803# or *1#, and Zong *8# or *5#. These are covered in detail in the network guides linked below.

Other useful telecom codes

  • MNP pre-check: SMS the text MNP to 667.
  • Network of a number: SMS N 03xx3456789 to 76367 (about Rs 2 plus tax).
  • SIMs on your CNIC: SMS your 13-digit CNIC to 668 or use cnic.sims.pk.
  • PTA helpline: 0800-55055 for general telecom complaints.

These services are for your own CNIC and numbers. Do not use them to look up someone else's details.

Packages, offers and subscriptions

The self-care menus also let you review active bundles, data add-ons and value-added subscriptions. It is worth checking these every few weeks, because an old subscription can quietly reduce your balance. If you see a service you did not subscribe to, use the menu to unsubscribe or ask the network's helpline to remove it.

If the menu does not respond

  • Restart the phone and dial the code again.
  • Reseat the SIM and wait for the network bars.
  • Check call settings for a block on USSD or short codes.
  • Try the network's app instead, since app menus often work when USSD is slow.

If the code still fails, confirm the current code with the operator or the PTA rather than relying on an old list. Short codes do change.

Watch out for fraud

Never share an OTP, a SIM code or a CNIC photo with anyone who contacts you first, even if they claim to be from your network. Genuine staff do not ask for OTPs over the phone. If a caller says your SIM will be blocked unless you share a code, that is a scam. Hang up, then call the operator's official helpline yourself if you are worried.

USSD codes and helplines can change with each update. If a code does not work, check the network's official website or the PTA before assuming it is wrong. This article is general information and not a substitute for operator guidance.

Frequently asked questions

What is the balance check code in Pakistan?
Each network uses its own self-care code: Jazz and Telenor commonly *111#, Ufone *706#, and Zong *102#. Follow the on-screen menu and confirm with the network.
How do I check my mobile data balance?
Dial your network's self-care code and choose the data or bundle option in the menu. The exact option can change, so read the menu carefully.
Are USSD codes free?
Most balance and data check menus are free, but some actions or queries may be chargeable. Check the menu wording before confirming.
What is the PTA helpline?
The PTA helpline is 0800-55055 for general telecom complaints and enquiries.
